items.stem: A Power Pages site must let signed-in members see only their own related records. Which table-permission access type fits?

options.rationale: Correct: Contact access scopes records to those related to the signed-in user's contact.
Global access exposes all records in the table to the web role.
Anonymous access is for unauthenticated users and does not scope to a signed-in member.
Without a table permission, users cannot access the records at all.

items.explanation: Correct: Contact access scopes records to those related to the signed-in user's contact.

items.stem: Why is client-side JavaScript filtering not an acceptable security boundary in Power Pages?

options.text: Users can bypass or modify it, so authorization must be enforced server-side
options.rationale: Correct: client-side filters can be bypassed; table permissions enforce authorization server-side.
Client filtering does not disable the Web API.
Client filtering does not alter table-permission access types.

items.explanation: Correct: client-side filters can be bypassed; table permissions enforce authorization server-side.

items.stem: Which TWO are correct about Power Pages security? (Select TWO)

options.text: Table permissions must be associated with web roles to grant data access
options.rationale: Correct: access to Dataverse records is granted by table permissions tied to web roles.

options.text: Granting the Anonymous users web role access to a table exposes that data to anyone
options.rationale: Correct: anonymous table permissions make the data visible to any visitor.

options.text: Hiding a page from navigation secures the page
options.rationale: Hiding from navigation is not security; page permissions are required.

options.text: Site visibility defaults to public on creation
options.rationale: Sites default to private/internal until explicitly made public.

items.explanation: Correct: access to Dataverse records is granted by table permissions tied to web roles.
